title: ‘The Secret Agent’ Director Kleber Mendonça Filho to Be Patron of Marrakech Film Festival’s Atlas Workshops
description: Brazilian filmmaker Kleber Mendonça Filho, best known for “The Secret Agent,” will be the patron – serving as a mentor to the filmmakers – of the 9
body:
Brazilian filmmaker Kleber Mendonça Filho, best known for “The Secret Agent,” will be the patron – serving as a mentor to the filmmakers – of the 9th edition of the Atlas Workshops, the Marrakech Film Festival’s professional platform dedicated to the development of Moroccan, Arab and African cinema, which takes place from Nov. 22 to 26.

	Mendonça Filho made his mark on the international scene with “Neighboring Sounds” (2012), “Aquarius” (2016) and “Bacurau on the Map” (2019), which won the Jury Prize at Cannes. His most recent film, “The Secret Agent” (2025), won the award for best director at Cannes before going on to win two Golden Globes and receive four Academy Award nominations this year.
	

	Mendonça Filho said, “Listening to new ideas and understanding the aspirations of new generations of filmmakers is a source of inspiration for my own work.


	“And all of this in Marrakech, such a fascinating city, which hosts such an exceptional film festival. Last year, during my Conversation at the festival, I was asked whether I had ever planned to shoot a film in this city. Serving as the patron of the Atlas Workshops makes me feel as though I’m witnessing, right before my eyes, the birth of new films.”

	Selected from among 320 projects in development and 90 films in production or post-production, this edition’s 30 projects and films fall into three categories: 14 projects in development, 11 films in production or post-production, and five projects in the Atlas Close-Ups section, which is dedicated to Moroccan cinema.

	The 14 countries that are represented are Algeria, Cabo Verde, Egypt, Ethiopia, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Palestine, Rwanda, Senegal, Sudan, Syria and Tunisia.
	

	The selection of projects in development includes 12 fiction films and two documentaries, of which six are debut feature-length films.

	Several of the projects are headed by filmmakers who have already won attention with their previous films: Amjad Abu Alala (“You Will Die at Twenty”), Laila Abbas (“Thank You for Banking With Us”), Meryem Benm’Barek (“Sofia,” “Behind the Palm Trees”), Sofia Alaoui (“Animalia”) and Yasmine Benkiran (“Queens”).

	Of the 11 films in production or post-production—including five debut feature-length films—four received development support from the Atlas Workshops: Samuel Ishimwe’s “Seasons of the Weary Kind” (Rwanda), selected in 2019; Alaa Eddine Aljem’s “Eldorado” (Morocco), selected in 2020; Yoro Mbaye’s “Fagadaga” (Senegal), selected in 2022; and Ismaël El Iraki’s “Wolfmother” (Morocco), selected in 2023.

	The Atlas Close-Ups program features five Moroccan projects, including four fiction films and one documentary.

	Atlas Station: A selection of producers and short films in post-production from MoroccoConceived to support young Moroccan professionals, this year’s Atlas Station welcomes eight filmmakers selected from among 30 applicants. In meetings and exchanges with international professionals, these four women and four men will participate in a professional development program focused on various aspects of film production.

	The program also provides support for five Moroccan short films in post-production—four fiction and one documentary—selected from among 24 submissions. The selected filmmaking teams will receive support tailored to the needs of their film, particularly in terms of final editing and distribution.

	The Atlas Programs—an initiative supporting Moroccan, Arab, and African cinemaFounded in 2018, the Atlas Workshops now fall under the Atlas Programs, which gathers together the professional initiatives of the Marrakech Film Festival.

	Atlas Press, Atlas Distribution MeetingsAtlas Press supports the development of film criticism, while the Atlas Distribution Meetings brings together some 60 professionals from Africa, the Arab world and Europe to foster networking and the circulation of films. The Atlas Distribution Awards rounds out this initiative by providing support for the distribution of films.
	

	The Atlas Workshops, Atlas Station and Atlas Distribution Meetings take place in Marrakech from Nov. 22 to 26, while Atlas Press takes place from Nov. 23 to 27.

title: Selena Gomez Reveals Vaping Nicotine Changed Her Voice: ‘It’s Not Worth It’
description:
Selena Gomez said heavy nicotine vaping has changed her voice, and told fans she has now quit the habit.

	The singer, actor and Rare Beauty founde
body:
Selena Gomez said heavy nicotine vaping has changed her voice, and told fans she has now quit the habit.

	The singer, actor and Rare Beauty founder, 34, spoke about it in a video of roughly a minute posted to her Instagram Story on Sunday.

	“I’m not going to be able to change my voice,” Gomez said. “I vaped nicotine a lot. Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it, or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid, and it’s changed my voice.”
	

	Gomez added that she understood if some fans didn’t like listening to her voice, and told them they were free to tune out.


	She said she was excited to have stopped and hoped she could keep it up, though it was hard.

	“But I know if you are going through something, you can get through it too,” she said. “It sucks.”

	Gomez did not cite vaping when she answered repeated fan questions about her voice during an Instagram Live session last December. At the time, she said her throat sometimes swells on the inside.

	Gomez has been open about her health over the years. She has lupus and received a kidney transplant in 2017, and she has spoken publicly about her bipolar disorder diagnosis, including in the 2022 documentary “Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me.”

	She stars in and executive produces the Hulu comedy series “Only Murders in the Building” alongside Steve Martin and Martin Short. The show returns Dec. 8 for its sixth season, which moves the action to London under the title “Only Murders in London.” She launched her cosmetics brand Rare Beauty in 2020.

schema.headline: Selena Gomez Reveals Vaping Nicotine Changed Her Voice: ‘It’s Not Worth It’

title: Psychological Horror ‘Henry’s Ebb,’ Starring ‘Widow’s Bay’s’ Kingston Rumi Southwick, Boarded by Bridge Independent (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Bridge Independent has boarded psychological horror film “Henry’s Ebb,” which stars Kingston Rumi Southwick, one of the stars of “Widow’s Bay.” The
body:
Bridge Independent has boarded psychological horror film “Henry’s Ebb,” which stars Kingston Rumi Southwick, one of the stars of “Widow’s Bay.” The film makes its world premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival. 

	“Henry’s Ebb,” written and directed by Thomas Mendolia in his feature debut, also stars Banks Repeta (“The Black Phone”), Ashley Shelton and Will Holland, with supporting performances from Rebecca Koon and Austin Willard.
	

	The film follows Henry, a boy who flees his troubled home in search of the father he barely remembers, accompanied by Ebb, the imaginary friend Henry created to help him survive a tumultuous childhood. But as their journey leads them through the backroads of the American South, Ebb’s protection becomes increasingly controlling, forcing Henry to question the companion he has always trusted.


	Bill Straus of Bridge Independent is handling domestic sales, with Logan Taylor of New Ratio Films serving as sales and distribution consultant.

	The film is produced by Ford Films’ Lucas Ford and Joey LePage, with Tony Tehle and Irina Slepneva serving as co-producers.

	“Henry’s Ebb” was previously selected for the Frontières Buyers Showcase at the Marché du Film during the Cannes Film Festival.

	The film will have its U.S. premiere at Cucalorus Film Festival in North Carolina, where the production was filmed and set.

	In a statement, Mendolia spoke about Elkin, North Carolina, the town in which he grew up and where he shot the film: “Elkin exists in my mind as both magical and painful, and that duality felt essential to the story. I wrote it around real locations from my memory, and knew that shooting here was crucial. Henry moves through a world that is full of wonder, but also shaped by the complicated lives of the adults around him. Setting the film there allowed those two feelings to coexist in the same space.”

title: ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho’s ‘Paradise Lost’ Clinches 118-Country Sales Ahead of Hawai‘i Festival U.S. Bow
description: “Paradise Lost,” the new psychological thriller by “Train to Busan” filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho, has been sold to 118 countries and will have its U.S. p
body:
“Paradise Lost,” the new psychological thriller by “Train to Busan” filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho, has been sold to 118 countries and will have its U.S. premiere at the 46th Hawai‘i International Film Festival. It will play in the Spotlight on Korea section on Nov. 1 and 4.

	CJ ENM, which is handling international sales, said overseas sales revenue alone had already topped the picture’s net production budget. The company put the result down to buyers’ faith in Yeon as a filmmaker and to the reach of a distribution network it has built over years of selling Korean films abroad.
	

	“The film combines a distinctive premise with a deeply felt exploration of family and motherhood,” said a representative of CJ ENM’s international distribution team. “These universal emotions are resonating across cultures and generating strong interest in international markets.”


	Kim Hyun-joo plays Ryu So-young, whose son vanished nine years before the story begins, along with a busload of children headed to camp. The boy, Ryu Sun-woo, had long been given up for dead. Then he comes home.

	Kim has worked with Yeon several times before. Bae Hyeon-seong plays Sun-woo in his first lead role in a feature film, and the knotty relationship between mother and son sits at the heart of the film.

	The Hawai‘i slot extends a festival run that has already taken in Toronto and Busan. At the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, the film played in the Special Presentations section and sold out all four of its official screenings, roughly 2,300 seats in total. It then screened as a Gala Presentation at the 31st Busan International Film Festival, where its four screenings also sold out.
	

	HIFF focuses on cinema from Asia and the Pacific and uses film to encourage cross-cultural exchange. This year’s edition will run Oct. 21 to Nov. 15 at venues around the state’s islands.

	“Paradise Lost” is produced by Wowpoint and presented by Wowpoint and CJ ENM. It will open in South Korean cinemas on Oct. 21, with CJ ENM distributing at home. Taiwan will follow on Oct. 23 and Singapore on Nov. 5. Well Go USA will release the film in North America on Nov. 6, the same day it opens in Vietnam, and Indonesia is set for Nov. 13.

schema.headline: ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho’s ‘Paradise Lost’ Clinches 118-Country Sales Ahead of Hawai‘i Festival U.S. Bow

title: Korea Box Office: Anime Sensation ‘Chiikawa’ Dominates Weekend
description: Japanese animated phenomenon “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” tightened its grip on the South Korean box office over the week
body:
Japanese animated phenomenon “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” tightened its grip on the South Korean box office over the weekend of Oct. 16–18, commanding more than 42% of nationwide ticket revenue in its third frame. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Toho-distributed fantasy feature generated $2.8 million from 378,474 admissions across 1,181 screens, accounting for a dominant 42.7% of the weekend market.
	

	Directed by Kei Oikawa and adapted from the popular manga by Nagano, the animated adventure follows the titular small character and companions traveling to an island paradise before confronting a mysterious aquatic legend. The release has lifted its cumulative South Korean gross to $14 million from 1,828,909 total admissions since its Sep. 30 launch.


	Director Hur Jin-ho’s controversial political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” held second place, pulling in $1 million from 140,017 admissions across 1,104 screens to capture 15.5% of the weekend market. Distributed by Hive Media Corp, the period drama reconstructs the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee and stars Yu Hae-jin, Park Hae-il, and Lee Min-ho as investigators probing inconsistencies in the official state inquiry.

	The production’s commercial run continues against persistent political blowback and legal challenges, with conservative civic organizations and bereaved family groups filing defamation complaints alleging historical distortion over its suggestion of internal state culpability in the shooting that killed First Lady Yuk Young-soo. Despite protests that previously disrupted promotional appearances and prompted 19 local film industry guilds to issue a joint statement defending cinematic expression, the title has crossed the three-million-ticket threshold, lifting its cume to $23.7 million from 3,249,174 admissions since its Sep. 23 rollout.
	

	CJ ENM’s gambling crime drama “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” maintained third place in its fourth weekend, generating $731,309 from 94,314 admissions across 789 screens for a 10.8% share of receipts. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the franchise has grossed $14.3 million from 1,911,190 viewers.

	Universal’s “The Odyssey” finished in fourth place in its eleventh weekend, drawing $580,011 from 52,439 admissions across 481 screens to take 8.6% of the frame. The Christopher Nolan-directed epic pushed its haul to $104.1 million from 12,267,696 admissions since opening on Aug. 5.

	20th Century Studios’ ocean survival thriller “Whalefall” debuted in fifth place, earning $300,004 from 38,637 admissions across 621 screens for 4.4% of the market. Since its mid-week rollout on Oct. 14, the film has accumulated $421,412 from 56,363 viewers.

	Director Kore-eda Hirokazu’s live-action manga drama “Look Back” took sixth place in its sophomore frame, taking $194,574 from 24,614 admissions across 271 screens, bringing its cumulative run to $829,170 from 105,345 viewers.

	Locus Animation’s local animated adventure “Guardians of the Video Game” opened in seventh place, collecting $165,350 from 22,427 admissions across 566 screens. Adapted from Gasfard’s popular Naver webtoon, the animated fantasy follows an elite game-world administrator demoted to managing a retro mobile video game, generating $295,340 from 42,647 admissions since its Oct. 14 premiere.

	Paramount Pictures and Legendary Entertainment’s video game adaptation “Street Fighter” debuted in eighth place with $122,148 from 16,813 admissions across 523 screens. The live-action franchise reboot has grossed $238,799 from 34,920 admissions following its Oct. 14 bow.

	Japanese supernatural chiller “The Mouths,” directed by Takashi Shimizu, took ninth place in its second weekend, earning $110,302 from 14,991 admissions across 245 screens for a cumulative total of $569,462 from 77,114 viewers.

	Rounding out the top ten, Lotte Entertainment’s action fantasy “Reawakened Man,” starring Koo Kyo-hwan, took $73,714 from 10,211 admissions across 292 screens, lifting its total to $2.4 million from 326,734 admissions.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $6.7 million, down from last week’s $10.5 million.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: Anime Sensation ‘Chiikawa’ Dominates Weekend

title: ‘Barry Loser’ Animated Series, Based on Bestselling U.K. Children’s Books, Finds Italian Partners Ahead of Rome’s MIA Market (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Barry Loser,” the award-winning, million-selling children’s book series from creator Jim Smith, is being adapted into an animated series by the U.
body:
“Barry Loser,” the award-winning, million-selling children’s book series from creator Jim Smith, is being adapted into an animated series by the U.K.’s Big Little Fish Television and Italian co-producer Frog Head.

	It’s one of the projects that will be pitched to industry reps during the newly launched Animation Series Gap-Financing Market at Rome’s MIA Market.

	Based on the Roald Dahl Funny Prize-winning book series that’s been translated into 17 languages, the show – which comprises 52 episodes, each 11 minutes long – follows the comic misadventures of Barry Loser, a lovable middle-schooler with a wonderfully warped imagination. The series, which aims to go into production in 2027, has been picked up in the U.K. by ITVX Kids.
	

	Speaking to Variety ahead of MIA, Big Little Fish CEO Mark Procter described the show as a “passion project” — and one that hits close to home.


	“About three years ago, ‘Barry Loser’ was my boy’s favorite title,” said the veteran TV exec. “We were devouring these books every night. He couldn’t get his hands on them fast enough. It would be a joy to lift that from the page and turn it into a TV franchise.”

	Launched in 2019, Big Little Fish Television is best known for its catalog of unscripted documentary, though both Procter and COO Georgina Surtees have worked extensively in children’s TV, including both live-action and animation. In 2023, the company produced the 20-part scripted reality family series “Meet the McQueens” for CBBC, and is currently developing a slate of pre-school and older kids’ programming based on both in-house and licensed IP.
	

	Created by Smith, the “Barry Loser” franchise includes 11 books and graphic novels that have sold more than a million copies worldwide. “We’re starting from a good place. The characters are well-rounded. There’s some really funny personalities in there. His home life, his friends and school,” said Procter. “All of those incredible characters and worlds that already exist give us endless opportunities to have a returnable series.”

	Set in Mogden, U.K., which is described by the producers as “an ordinary town [with] an extraordinary imagination,” “Barry Loser” turns on the 10-year-old’s ability to make something as mundane as a trip to the store or a visit to grandma’s seem like an epic, over-the-top adventure.

	“A lot of the charm of this is Barry’s imagination,” said Procter. “We’re going to stay faithful to the books with a loose, hand-drawn style in 2D. With that comes the opportunity for us to unleash Barry’s imagination and go anywhere with it.

	“He lives in an everyday, ordinary town that kids will relate to, but he finds extraordinary adventures within these worlds,” Procter continued. “His everyday challenges lead to fantastical adventures.”

	The series is co-produced by Frog Head, an Italian specialist in audiovisual, sound design and animation, and illustrated by Florence-based DogHead Animation, which was founded in 2019 by Movimenti Production and is now a subsidiary of Banijay Kids & Family.

	The partnership sprung from a fruitful meeting at MipJunior several years back, said Procter, with the Italians making an irresistible pitch that included photos of the “Barry Loser” series on their own children’s bookshelves.

	“That level of enthusiasm matched our own,” he said. “DogHead’s back catalog and experience in producing fast-paced, gag-filled, quick, funny children’s shows — it felt immediately like we were meant to be.”

	Given the challenges in financing animated TV series, Surtees acknowledged that accessing Italy’s 40% tax credit was “a big draw,” which combined with the U.K. tax credit gives the producers a leg up heading into the MIA market.

	“We’re exploring other co-pro partners that can also bring tax credits to the table to help bridge the deficit gap,” she said, estimating that 60-70% of the budget for “Barry Loser” is already in place. “If we are able to bridge that deficit gap, we are ready to go.” The producers are aiming to close financing by the end of Q1 in 2027 and go into production at the beginning of Q2.
	

	While shoring up the show’s financing is the main goal at this year’s MIA Market, Procter said the team behind “Barry Loser” is just as excited to find creative partners to help the series on its journey to the screen.

	“I love the books and ITV love the books. Our Italian co-producers and animators love the idea of it. But it would also be wonderful to sit down and go through the creative process with European partners to ensure that what we love about this works for them, too,” he said. 

	“We have all of these wonderful worlds and characters. But the idea of sitting down and presenting and then adapting to local needs and wants — all of that is part of the creative development process that we’re really excited to move into,” he continued. “We are hopeful that out of MIA we have some really interesting conversations, to have one or two networks come on board to co-produce to finally get this over the line so that I can be the best dad in the world.”

	Rome’s MIA Market runs Oct. 19 – 23.

title: Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua Find Their JxJ Duo Sound on ‘Dreamscape’: ‘Right in the Middle Between Strong and Subtle’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: For more than a decade, Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua have shared the spotlight with 11 bandmates in one of K-pop’s best-selling groups. Now they
body:
For more than a decade, Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua have shared the spotlight with 11 bandmates in one of K-pop’s best-selling groups. Now they get it to themselves with “Dreamscape,” their first album as the duo JxJ.

	The record is also Jeonghan’s first new music since he completed South Korea’s mandatory military service this summer. While he served, Seventeen kept performing without him, and at times he watched his bandmates from the audience, among the group’s fans, known as Carats. Joshua spent the same stretch producing songs of his own and sending them to their company.
	

	The pair met as trainees and recorded the duet “Falling for U” for the 2018 special album “Director’s Cut,” but JxJ is the first project built entirely around the two of them.


	Joshua says their company first suggested they collaborate together. “After giving it some thought, we’ve been together for so long, and we really wanted to show a different side to ourselves,” he says. “Sides that we haven’t shown as a whole group, as Seventeen, so we thought it was going to be fun. And a lot of our fans actually like our chemistry, the chemistry that the two of us have.”

	Jeonghan says that with several members away on military service, those who remained talked with the company about how to keep bringing Carats new music. “We thought that it would be a really exciting project, so that’s how it came to life.”

	Seventeen debuted in 2015 under Pledis Entertainment, now part of Hybe, with 13 members split into hip-hop, vocal and performance teams. It holds the record for the highest-selling K-pop album, “FML,” and was the first K-pop act to sell more than 5 million copies of an album in its first week. All 13 members renewed their Pledis contracts this summer, the second time the full group has re-signed. Military service has thinned the lineup, though. Six members are currently serving, and Seungkwan and Dino enlist together on Oct. 26. That leaves five active members: Jeonghan, Joshua, S.Coups, Jun and The8. Jeonghan and Joshua both sing in the vocal team, and JxJ is the group’s seventh unit.
	

	“The exhilaration and the Carats screaming, cheering, their love, the spotlight – everything is something that you can only enjoy on stage,” Jeonghan tells Variety. “So I missed those moments on stage. I just wanted to get ready after finishing my military service, prep myself, and get back on there as soon as possible.”

	He says he came out of the service having grown more as a person than as an artist. “When I was in the military, in my workplace, I felt so much love, consideration, respect, and those heartfelt feelings for other people. I just wanted to weave that into the music, and I just hope that that will show when the listeners and our beloved Carats are listening to our music.”

	Of everything he felt in that time, warmth struck him hardest, and he came to see it as “a form of love.” It is the one thing, he says, he doesn’t want to lose sight of.

	The songs Joshua handed over made an impression. “They were really surprised with the work that I’ve done,” he says of the company. “I think my company knew more about my personal taste after I gave them what I produced.”

	Jeonghan hadn’t known that Joshua was so interested in producing. “When we started working on this album, I was amazed by how clear an idea he had in his mind about the musical direction that we should have moving forward. It seemed like he gave it a lot of thought and has confidence in it.”

	The credits bear that out. Joshua co-wrote and co-composed his solo track, the alternative rock song “Not Personal,” and has a lyric credit on the closer, “No Looking Back.” Jeonghan co-wrote the lyrics for his own solo, the electro-house track “Coloring.”

	Joshua had his own surprise. With a tour to follow the album’s promotions, Jeonghan had been mapping out the stage show. “I didn’t know he was thinking that much about the concert performances and how we should showcase our abilities through the concerts,” Joshua says. “So that was really interesting.”

	The two didn’t start out agreeing on what JxJ should sound like. “He wanted to showcase a more… what would you call it? A more aggressive… well, not aggressive, but a stronger side, and I wanted to show a subtle, mature version of ourselves,” Joshua says. “Eventually, we met at the middle and came out with the song ‘12 O’Clock,’ which is right in the middle between strong and subtle.”
	

	Getting there took three or four candidates for the title track. One started out as a house song and was then reworked as a band track. The final pick sits between the two. “I think this album was more meaningful, not so much in that we were attempting new tries, but in that we were able to expand our spectrum and touch on different genres that we didn’t explore in the past,” Jeonghan says.

	“12 O’Clock” is a dance-rock track built on ’70s and ’80s disco and funk. Its title plays on noon and midnight: one hour for chasing goals in waking life, the other for the fantasies of sleep. In the video, the pair wander through warped train carriages and rooms with no way out, following a mythical creature that is part peacock, part Ouroboros. The seven-track album opens with the house song “Like You,” passes through R&B and soul, and ends on the raw band sound of “No Looking Back.” Jeonghan says that range gives the record an immersive, dreamlike feel, and the choreography is being built to match. “We just really wanted the whole album to feel like a journey between traveling through dreams and reality,” Joshua says.

	For Joshua, the bigger change from Seventeen is how much he gets to sing. Within a 13-member group, and a five-member vocal team, his parts are short. “Even if it lasts long, it’s like five seconds. But as a unit, we could show more of our vocals.”

	Making his career far from home was its own adjustment. Joshua grew up in Los Angeles. When he first arrived in Korea, he struggled with customs such as bowing and speaking in honorifics to elders. Thirteen years on, Korea feels like home, and he has watched the world catch up with it. “Even if I was American in America, it was really hard for me to fit in at first because of the differences and nobody knew anything about Korea at that time,” he says. “But now, it’s the new cool thing.”

	Jeonghan says Seventeen’s global scale brings freedom and pressure hand in hand. “Of course, there’s the faith and the trust that our fans place in us, and this helps us explore various genres and take on new challenges. But at the same time, there’s the pressure to live up to their expectations. The pressure is always there, and that’s why we’re always trying harder and having so many meetings and practicing really hard.”
	

	Joshua is waiting to see how fans respond before saying whether JxJ goes beyond one album. “We won’t know where this will take us until we get there” he says. Jeonghan sounds more sure. He says the pair saw the unit’s potential while preparing “Dreamscape” and came away feeling “this unit will definitely have something else to offer, something new to bring to the table.”

	The album may be named for dreams, but Jeonghan says he didn’t make it to chase one. He sees it as the pair’s first album since entering their 30s. “I just wanted to showcase myself as a grown, more mature artist,” he says.

	Working on JxJ showed Joshua how much he likes having a hand in his own music, and he says he can’t wait to make more personal work of his own. He has other plans too. “I’m also taking acting classes, so hopefully in the future I could be in a future acting project,” Joshua says. “That’d be really cool.”

	Jeonghan says he thinks less about a next goal than about the fans already there. “I am just so grateful for all the love and support that our fans, Carats, are sending. So I just want to show them great music, bring them good music, and share great moments with them, and just keep growing together.”

schema.headline: Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua Find Their JxJ Duo Sound on ‘Dreamscape’: ‘Right in the Middle Between Strong and Subtle’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Tallinn Baltic Event: New Movie From Darko Lungulov and Ernestas Jankauskas, Plus Titles Directed by Rising Talents Josh Trigg, Marina Palacio and Many More
description: Tribeca-winning helmer Darko Lungulov, behind Serbia’s Oscar candidate “Here and There,” and Lithuania’s Ernestas Jankauskas (“Troll Farm,” “I Am F
body:
Tribeca-winning helmer Darko Lungulov, behind Serbia’s Oscar candidate “Here and There,” and Lithuania’s Ernestas Jankauskas (“Troll Farm,” “I Am Fine, Thanks,” “Sasha Was Here”) are among a handful of seasoned filmmakers set to pitch their works in progress at Tallinn’s Baltic Event industry showcase Nov. 19, next to a swathe of exciting new voices.Those take in Bafta-nominated Welsh helmer Josh Trigg, Naomi Kawase’s protégé, coming to Tallinn with the Japanese language “Leopard Spots,” and Basque newcomer Marina Palacio with “And Thus It Will Go On” produced by Gariza Films (“Sisters,” “20,000 Species of Bees”). Meanwhile Lithuanian talent to watch and American Film Institute graduate Saulius Baradinskas, Golden Lion candidate in Venice for his short “Techno Mama,” will pitch his feature debut “Concrete Music,” a crime drama and musical set in 1990s post-Soviet Lithuania.Split across the Baltic Event Works in Progress, International Works in Progress and Just Film Works in Progress for kids and youth, this year’s rich works in progress lineup takes in 16 projects in production or post-production, selected from more than 100 submissions from all around the world.“The final selection is a great blend of different genres from psychological dramas to dark comedies and satiric self-reflections,” said works in progress co-managers Kärt Väinola and Helen Räim, who received a slew of entries from Southeast, Central Europe, Latin America and Spain. One Basque project “And So It Will Go On,” made it into the International Works in Progress, a nice addition said the co-honchos as the Basque region is spotlighted at Tallinn’s Black Nights Film Festival.Turning on overarching themes, Väinola and Räim said “the theme of family and especially the bond between parent and child runs through the whole selection, as a source of both fear and freedom.”


	They also pointed at mortality and loss, “treated with rare lightness in several films,” notably in the dark comedies “A Midnight Pilgrimage,” “Marry Then Die,” “Burlaks” and “The Elderly Store,” or in the drama with fantasy elements “The Reef.” “Time and memory also appear as important central subjects in “And So It Will Go On,” and “Luci Looped in Limbo,” they observed.
	

	For the first time, all 16 works in progress will be pitched the same day — Thursday Nov. 19 — in the morning and early afternoon to leave the filmmakers more time to discuss, mingle and create new partnerships before the Baltic Event closing ceremony Nov. 20.

	Full rundown of the works in progress:
	

	International Works in Progress

	“And Thus It Will Go On” (“Y así seguirán las cosas,” Marina Palacio, Spain)

	Directorial debut of rising talent Palacio, produced by high-profile Basque outfit Gariza Films (“20,000 Species of Bees,” “Sisters”). Won “most promising project” at Tallinn-Baltic Event Script Pool 2022.Hybrid pic shot over several years in which a child, Germán, lives isolate in a village, surrounded by adults and elderly people. Once reunited with his old friends in the endless fields, play becomes his way of discovering and understanding life. “Marina’s cinematic vision and storytelling skills, makes this movie a coming of age full of magic, truly hypnotic,” says exec producer Ana Angulo Umaran.

	“Leopard Spots” (Josh Trigg, Japan, U.K.)



	

									Courtesy of On Par Productions
	



	Sophomore pic from Welsh helmer Trigg, after his breakthrough film, the Bafta-nominated “Satu-Year of the Rabbit.” Produced by On Par Productions, Kingyo Films, Geronimo Boy Film. Following “Satu-Year of the Rabbit”’s top accolade at the Nara Int’l Film Festival, prominent Japanese helmer Naomi Kawase and Nara founder invited Trigg to direct “Leopard Spots” in Japan. Shot in 16mm in a small factory town in Nara, the pic “combines British social-realist sensibility with contemplative Japanese cinema,” says Toby Cameron who produces with Aiko Flores Yoshioka, Ruth Yoshie Linton. The story turns on single mother Lilly who grapples to keep her daughter close in a bitter-sweet tale of failed redemption.

	“Luci Looped in Limbo” (Théo Gottlieb, France)



	

									Courtesy of Hiersoir Films
	



	Feature debut of rising talent Gottlieb, starring Luzja Richter (“Phantom Thread,” “Vikings: Valhalla”) Bella Kim (“Winter in Sokcho”) and seasoned actor Pascal Grégory (“One Fine Morning,” “La vie en rose”).

	Produced by Yoel Servadio for Hiersoir Films, in co-production with 84 Films.Luci, a physicist obsessed with changing the past, must learn to accept the present.

	This is a pic “rooted in a deeply personal story that explores universal themes of love, loss and acceptance, with the ambition of resonating with a broad international audience,” says Servadio. “Bringing together a French and Korean cast in a multilingual narrative, it blends science fiction with an intimate love story unfolding across a lifetime. Rather than using time travel and sci-fi as a spectacle, the film explores our desire to hold on to what inevitably changes, combining a high-concept premise with emotional depth and a distinctive multicultural identity.”
	

	“Požari” (“Fires,” Nina Tratnik, Montenegro, Albania, Serbia)

	Debut feature. As wildfires close in on Podgorica, Ana (18) has to take care of her dying grandmother, secretly recording her parents on her phone, and uncovering the desires and long-buried tensions tearing her family apart. Produced by Code Blue production with Era Film, Cinnamon-CinneRent, Radio & Television Montenegro.

	“Without You” (“Uden Dig,” Nil Holst-Jensen, Denmark)

	Psychological thriller from the director of the TV series “Where Were You.” Produced by Daniel Mühlendorph for Hyæne Film. Sine feels trapped by motherhood due to her demanding daughter, Ida. When Ida suddenly disappears, Sine’s world is shattered, yet her lost freedom, old friends, and acting career unexpectedly return. Everything she ever wanted comes within reach, as long as Ida doesn’t return.

	“The Elderly Store,” (Karylar dukonu,” Amanbek Azhymat, Kyrgyzstan)

	Sophomore feature by Azhymat whose debut “Backstage Madness” screened at PÖFF in 2025. Absurd and darkly humorous drama, offering an unconventional take on aging, loneliness and human dignity. “At the center of the film is a paradoxical world in which an elderly person must prove his usefulness in order to earn the right to continue living,” says associate producer Elvira Mamytova.

	Baltic Event Works in Progress

	“A Midnight Pilgrimage” (“Öised rännakud,” Katrin Ruus, Estonia)

	Poetic tragicomedy from newcomer Ruus, written by Estonia’s prominent filmmaker Peeter Urbla, recipient of a PÖFF Lifetime Achievement in 2022. Urbla and Sander Lebreht produce for Exitfilm. When tragedy strikes, a carefree journalist must step up to anchor his family and rebuild his world. Toplining the cast are Indrek Sammul and Kristina Preimann. “Katrin Ruus looks at a man’s grief with patience and tenderness, and lets the audience stay with him long enough to understand him. At a time when everyone is asking where men fit in, this film doesn’t lecture. It listens,” says Lebrecht.

	“Marry Then Die” (“Apprecēties un mirt”, Elza Gauja, Latvia)
	

	Gauja who won best film at the Latvian Film Awards 2024 for “Postcard from Rome,” comes back with a dark romantic tragedy built around an unusual pact. Zigis, a charming drifter, will help Anya, a suicidal widow, to end her life, but only if they marry first! Produced by one of Latvia’s most established outfits VFS Films. “Elza Gauja’s distinctive directorial style-warm, playful and deeply attentive to human contradictions-allows difficult subjects to coexist naturally with humour and tenderness,” says Līva Vernere who produces with Uldis Cekulis. Pitched at the 2024 B.E. Co-Production Market.

	“Concrete Music” (“Betono muzika,” Saulius Baradinskas, Lithuania, Italy)



	

									Courtesy Viktoria Films
	



	Feature debut from one of Lithuania’s most exciting new voices, American Film Institute graduate Baradinskas, who’s short “Techno Mama” bowed in Venice. Crime drama and musical set in 1990s post-Soviet Lithuania starring Domantas Starkauskas. Musically gifted teenager Rokas, runs away from his mafia family to use music as a way to take revenge on his father, responsible for his mother’s death. Italy’s Andrea Gori (Lumen Films) co-produces; the music is composed by Andrea Boccadoro.“Burlaks,” (“Burlaki,” Gatis Ungurs, Latvia, Georgia)

	Mythological modern comedy by debut helmer Ungurs about flawed hero Miervalds, a sawmill worker who, disgusted by his boring life, embarks on a journey to a mythical mountain village where he becomes a wager between God and the Devil.Kristele Pudane -Cannes Latvian Producer on the Move 2025- produces with Dace Siatkovska for Sunday Rebel Films, in co-production with Georgia’s Half Alien Films.

	“Paraiso, Outer Space,” (Carlos E. Lesmes, Estonia)

	Experimental and personal film by Colombia-born Estonia-based Lesmes whose doc “A Loss of Something Ever Felt,” premiered at Hot Docs 2020. “A walk in the Bardo illuminated by city lights, a sea of connections that look like people,” reads the logline.Produced by the helmer and Lili Pilt for Tin Can and Hare Films.Just Film Works in Progress

	“Uncle Egg,” (“Onkel Egg,” Torfinn Iversen, Norway, Germany)

	Sophomore pic by Norwegian writer/director Iversen, Crystal Bear nominated in 2017 with “Oskar’s America.”“Game of Thrones’ Kristofer Hivju stars as the titular character, the eccentric Uncle Egg, who travels to Germany with his nephew Hauk (12) from Northern Norway, to help him find his biological father. Martin Müller The search turns into quite a challenge as 25,000 men in Germany carry the same name. Produced by Fjordic film.

	“The Queen of England Stole My Parents” (“Anglijos karalienė pagrobė mano tėvus,” Ernestas Jankauskas, Lithuania)
	



	

									Courtesy of Dansu Films
	



	From one of Lithuania’s leading production and serving outlets Dansu Film, co-producer of Netflix’s “Clark” and producer of Lithuania’s first high-quality TV show “Troll Farm” helmed by Jankauskas. Feature spinoff of the helmer’s short film of the same name, which bagged best short at the Lithuanian Film Awards 2014. Deeply personal film about adoption co-penned by producer Gaibja Siurbyte -Jankauskas’ partner. Smiltė (10), an adopted girl embarks on a journey to save her biological parents from the Queen of England.

	“The film follows a girl in foster care through a magical, often absurd adventure. It’s funny, but it doesn’t look away from what she’s going through,” says Viktorija Rimkutė who produces with Siurbyte. The script is co-penned by Aleksandra Chmielewska.

	“The Reef” (“Strandgut,” Phillip Donnellon, Germany, Estonia, Finland)



	

									Credit: Antti Lahtinen
	



	From the director of the Palme d’or short film nominated “Bird in the Wire.”

	Adapted by Michael Kinirons from the novel ”Karikko” by Seita Vuorela. Produced by Eyrie Entertainment, in co-production with Stellar Film Tack Films, and Gretchenfilm, in association with Split Second Films Limited. Little Dream Pictures handles German distribution, Yle Finnish TV rights and Epsilon Film world sales.

	Producer Daniel Ehrenber says the pic uniquely “brings together two things that don’t often go hand in hand in films for young audiences: the excitement of a gripping adventure and an honest exploration of grief and loss. Inspired by the imaginative tradition of stories like “Peter Pan” and “The Brothers Lionheart,” it takes young audiences on a journey that is thrilling, mysterious and full of wonder, while gradually revealing a deeply emotional story at its heart.”

	“1970,” (Darko Lungulov, Serbia, Luxembourg, Hungary, Croatia)

	From the acclaimed director of “Here and There” (Best N.Y. Narrative at Tribeca), Karlovy Vary-selected “Monument to Michael Jackson.”

	Set in 1970 Yugoslavia, it follows Draško (13), who, abandoned by his parents, runs away with Erzika (16). Drifting from place to place, swept into anti–Vietnam War protests during Nixon’s visit, free love, wild rock concerts, and decadent parties, his journey home becomes an awakening to heartbreak, loss, and freedom. “Although set more than 50 years ago, it is very much a story about today as it takes us back to a time when young people believed in the possibility of changing the world,” said the helmer, who was inspired by his own childhood memories. “Set against the backdrop of Yugoslavia’s counterculture movement, this intimate coming-of-age story speaks to a new generation struggling to find its voice and its place in a world that often seems to offer little hope.” Produced by Lungulov and Snezana van Houwelingen for This and That Productions with Papa Films (Serbia), Mirage Film (Hungary), Samsa Film (Luxembourg), PomPom Film (Croatia).

	“All Girls,” (Всички момичета,” Boyana Avdjieva, Bulgaria)

	Social drama from actor-turn director Avdjieva who stars in it. Produced by On Pointe Productions. Avdjieva describes her pic as a “raw, distinctly female portrayal of adolescent friendship, the intensity of girlhood and the heartbreak of bonds that fall apart, set against the social realities of 2000s post-socialist Bulgaria as the country steps into the EU.”“Inspired by the events of the 2001 “Indigo” club tragedy in Sofia and similar recent cases in Europe, this independently made Bulgarian debut brings together exclusively young talent to tell a story of a generation’s fragile hope for a better future and the cost of continuing to believe in it,” she adds.

title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ Ranks No. 2 at Global Box Office as ‘Street Fighter’ Leads
description: Indian superstar Rajinikanth’s Tamil-language action comedy “Jailer 2” was the second-biggest film in the world over the Oct. 16–18 weekend, grossi
body:
Indian superstar Rajinikanth’s Tamil-language action comedy “Jailer 2” was the second-biggest film in the world over the Oct. 16–18 weekend, grossing $31.2 million, according to Rentrak estimates. Only Paramount’s “Street Fighter,” with $51.1 million, earned more.

	The Nelson Dilipkumar-directed sequel opened in India on, Oct. 15, and grossed an estimated INR224 crore ($23.5 million) across its four-day extended opening. That is the third-highest four-day start on record for a Tamil-language film, and effectively level with another Rajinikanth vehicle, “Coolie,” which managed INR224.25 crore ($23.6 million).
	

	The film began with $7 million on Thursday. Collections dipped on Friday before climbing back through the weekend, with Sunday bringing in $6.5 million.


	Tamil Nadu, the southern Indian state where the Tamil-language film industry is based, delivered the biggest share at $8.4 million. The neighboring southern Indian states of Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana supplied most of the remainder.

	In North America, where the film is distributed by Shloka Entertainments, “Jailer 2” grossed $3.2 million over the Friday-to-Sunday frame, debuting at No. 9, taking its total to $5.2 million. Shloka said the film crossed $2 million on its opening day in the territory.

	“Jailer 2” follows the 2023 hit “Jailer,” in which Rajinikanth played a retired prison warden drawn back into violence when an idol smuggler threatens his family. He returns as “Tiger” Muthuvel Pandian, with Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu and Mirnaa also reprising their roles. New to the franchise are Tamil actor S.J. Suryah as Bodhi Kalpak and Bollywood star Vidya Balan as Kaantha. Veteran Bollywood actor Mithun Chakraborty and Malayalam cinema actor Suraj Venjaramoodu also join the cast. Dilipkumar wrote and directed both films for Kalanithi Maran’s Sun Pictures, and Anirudh Ravichander again composed the music.
	

	The sequel also brings in stars from other Indian language industries for brief appearances. Malayalam cinema icon Mohanlal and Kannada star Shiva Rajkumar, both of whom made cameos in the first film, return as Mathew and Narasimha, and Bollywood veteran Jackie Shroff plays Kamdev. Hrithik Roshan turns up as Roddy. The scene reunites Roshan with Rajinikanth 40 years after the 1986 Hindi film “Bhagwan Dada,” in which Roshan appeared as a child. 

	Elsewhere on the global chart, Sony’s “Resident Evil” ranked third with $22.6 million, followed by Universal’s “Other Mommy” at $17.9 million and “Verity” at $17.6 million.

title: Busan Winner ‘Ria,’ Arvin Belarmino’s Folk-Punk Debut, Boards Lights On (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Ria,” Philippines filmmaker Arvin Belarmino’s debut feature about a young woman from the folk-punk scene who takes on a property developer to save
body:
“Ria,” Philippines filmmaker Arvin Belarmino’s debut feature about a young woman from the folk-punk scene who takes on a property developer to save her home, has been picked up by international sales company Lights On following its world premiere at the Busan International Film Festival.

	The film picked up the Heart of Eurasia Award after bowing in Busan.

	In the story, Ria teams up with her foster mother and their fellow punks to resist a merciless developer intent on tearing down their building. It is the last structure left standing in a neighborhood that has already been reduced to rubble.
	

	The film is a co-production between the Philippines, the Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Japan and Norway.


	“An ode to rebellion and a fierce cry against injustice, ‘Ria’ is a film that reminds us of cinema’s ability to resist, question, and confront the world around us. A film that deserves to travel far and connect with audiences across borders,” said Lights On co-founder and managing director Flavio Armone.

	Armone said the company was especially proud to see the project come together because it extends its relationship with Belarmino. The two previously worked together on “Agapito,” a Cannes-debuting short that Belarmino co-directed with Kyla Romero.

	“I’m so happy to be collaborating with Lights On. They’ve been part of my journey as a filmmaker, witnessing my growth from my short film to now bringing my feature film to life. There’s something so fulfilling about finding people who see your vision, believe in your stories, and grow alongside you,” said Belarmino.
	

	Producer Kristine De Leon said making the film had not been easy, adding: “Having people you can trust makes the journey a little lighter. That’s something I’ve found with Lights On.”

	Lights On’s slate also includes Polen Ly’s Cambodian feature “Becoming Human,” a 2025 Venice title, and “Hair, Paper, Water…,” from Nicolas Graux and Trương Minh Quý, which played Locarno the same year. “Becoming Human” is Cambodia’s Oscar submission this year.

title: Ecuador Priest Dies After Massive Crucifix Falls on Him During Livestreamed Mass
description:
Ecuador Catholic Priest
                          Dies After Cross Falls on Him Mid-Livestream
body:
Ecuador Catholic Priest
                          Dies After Cross Falls on Him Mid-Livestream
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 18, 2026
                
                            8:20 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 18, 2026
                                11:47 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Catholic priest in Ecuador has died after a massive crucifix came crashing down on him in the middle of a church service ... and the terrifying accident was captured on a livestream.
      
    
      
      Catholic priest Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was killed when a crucifix fell on him during a service in Ecuador. Congregants tried to help, but he died from his injuries. https://t.co/u2b4DaZPok
              @Breaking911
          
  
    
            Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading Mass at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil on Saturday, when roughly 27 minutes into the livestreamed service the large wooden cross mounted behind the altar suddenly came loose and fell onto him.
      
    
            The service was being broadcast live online, and footage captured the shocking moment the crucifix toppled forward ... striking the priest near the altar as he addressed worshippers.
      

            The sudden collapse brought the service to an abrupt halt, with people inside the church reacting to the horrifying scene and rushing to help.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed Sánchez Molinari's death Sunday in a statement to Instagram, mourning the loss of the parish priest and offering condolences to his loved ones and fellow members of the religious community.
      
    
            Sánchez Molinari served as pastor of the church and was a member of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Catholic religious order.
      
    
            It's unclear what caused the heavy crucifix to detach from the wall. Church officials have not publicly provided an explanation for the collapse.

title: Cindy Crawford Remembers Late Son Presley Gerber in Heartbreaking Tribute
description:
Cindy Crawford
                          Emotional Tribute to Late Son Presley
body:
Cindy Crawford
                          Emotional Tribute to Late Son Presley
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 18, 2026
                
                            10:31 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 18, 2026
                                12:06 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cindy Crawford is mourning the loss of her son Presley Gerber ... sharing an emotional tribute remembering the 27-year-old.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            The supermodel posted a black-and-white photo of Presley with what appear to be angel wings on Instagram Sunday, writing she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over his death ... and Kaia reposted her mom's heartbreaking message.
      
    
            Cindy wrote ... "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever."
      

            She went on to say the family is proud of the way Presley carried himself through life, particularly his kindness and vulnerability.
      
    
            Cindy also thanked everyone who has shown the family love and support during the devastating time ... including strangers who have reached out to share their condolences.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She ended the tribute with a heartbreaking message signed by herself, Presley's father Rande Gerber, and his sister Kaia Gerber, "Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia." Rande shared the same post to his account.
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Presley died Santa Monica sober living facility September 20, just hours after checking in. Police have been investigating his death as a suspected overdose, and no foul play is suspected.
      
    
            His autopsy was completed, but his official cause of death was deferred pending further investigation.
      
    
            Presley had also been open about his past struggles with substance abuse and mental health ... sharing some of his personal battles publicly over the years.
